brief.headline: Blackstone Nears Sale of Tokyo Office Tower to Daiwa for $1.9B
bullets: Infrastructure & Energy: Blackstone is in advanced talks to sell the office and retail space at Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho to funds managed by units of Daiwa Securities for around JPY 300 billion ($1.9 billion), according to sources who spoke with Mingtiandi.

Exits & Secondaries: Blackstone has told investors that Anthropic may receive a sub-investment-grade credit rating after its planned IPO, revising earlier expectations and potentially raising the AI company’s financing costs, according to a report by the Financial Times.

Private Credit: Apollo Global Management is launching European Credit Co, a €10bn ($11.2bn) private credit platform backed by investors including Abu Dhabi Investment Council, according to a report by Bloomberg.
Real Estate: Terra and Fortune International Group have secured a $220 million predevelopment loan for a waterfront luxury condo development on Key Biscayne near Miami, the developers announced.
Real Estate: Every Monday, Blackstone’s investment committee meets to decide what to buy.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,580.07 (down 1.8% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 19.4, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.98% (down 7 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.38 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.44%, near long-run norms (up 18 bps on the prior reading).
